newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures prices finish higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures prices finish higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Monday in line with a recent uptrend that is taking some strength from stronger physicals and natural gas prices, industry sources said.

November California Oregon Border (COB) settled 30 cents higher at $18.70 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $18.95, while December COB closed up 40 cents at $19.80 after trade as high as $19.90.
Traders said November COB broke resistance at $18.75, but at least one broker said the futures prices may ease off the upsurge Tuesday with some resistance Monday near $18.80 and $18.85 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds were steady to 30 cents higher.
November Palo Verde closed up 15 cents at $17.39 per MWh after trade as high as $17.50, whle December ended 20 cents higher at $17.85 per MWh after trade as high as $17.90.
Remaining COB deferreds were steady to 15 cents higher.
NYMEX said a total of 213 COB and 264 PV contracts traded Monday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
